headline: Margin expansion lifts profit as loan growth continues
summary_short: Revenue rose 7% y/y to $1.96 billion and net income climbed 20% y/y to $509 million, with diluted EPS up 26% y/y to $0.44 as net interest margin expanded 23bp to 2.89%. KeyCorp repurchased $341 million of shares during the quarter.
summary_long: Net interest income rose 9% y/y to $1.26 billion (TE) as deposit costs fell and maturing low-yield securities were reinvested at higher yields; margin expanded 23bp to 2.89%. Noninterest income rose 2% on trust/investment-services gains, offset by lower mortgage-servicing fees. Expenses rose 5%, mostly incentive-linked personnel costs. Provision for credit losses fell to $92 million on a $23 million reserve release, even as net charge-offs rose to 42bp and nonperforming loans reached 0.73% of period-end loans. CET1 fell 50bp y/y to 11.2% after $341 million of buybacks and a $0.205/share dividend. No numeric next-quarter guidance was given, beyond a CEO target of >15% ROTCE by year-end 2027.

drivers.explanation: CEO Gorman cited 7% revenue growth and about 130bp of y/y operating leverage, with investment-banking pipelines up 9% q/q and assets under management at a record $74 billion.
Release attributes the increase to a 9% y/y rise in net interest income (lower deposit costs, higher-yield reinvestment, favorable loan mix) plus a 2% rise in noninterest income.
Net income growth outpaced revenue growth as a 5% rise in noninterest expense was more than offset by higher revenue and a lower y/y credit-loss provision.
EPS growth of 26% y/y reflects higher net income combined with a 2.5% reduction in weighted diluted shares from buybacks.
Share count fell as the company repurchased $341 million of common stock in the quarter.
